writeup.headline: Repligen rates Hold: strong balance sheet, trend and news offset by a very high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Repligen scores 58, a Hold, because solid fundamentals and strong share-price momentum are weighed down by valuation. The balance sheet is the standout at 96, with net cash and cash covering debt 1.47 times, and the trend score of 87 reflects shares 54.2 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days and the price 5.1% below its 52-week high. Growth is decent at 56, with TTM revenue growth of 16.5%, though growth slowed by 2.9 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is moderate at 62, with a 53.8% gross margin, an 8.2% operating margin and a 14.3% FCF margin. Valuation scores just 4: in absolute terms the multiples are high (P/S 13.3x, P/FCF 93.1x, EV/EBIT 157.3x), and the stock is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 59 of the last 61 month-ends on P/FCF.
key_risks: A very high absolute valuation leaves little room for disappointment, with the FCF yield 3.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield.
Revenue growth is slowing, with the latest quarter at 11.9% year on year.
Integration risk from the BioLife acquisition, which also flatters reported growth with an inorganic tailwind of about 2.5 points.
Filtration weakness and soft gene therapy demand could weigh on results.
After a strong run, with the price 27.7% above its 200-day average, the shares are exposed to a pullback.
what_would_change: A 7-point rise in the score to 65 would move the rating to Buy, for example through re-accelerating organic growth or a better valuation score after a price pullback.
Wider operating margins lifting the quality score would also push the score toward Buy.
A 14-point fall to below 45 would mean Sell, for example if momentum reverses and the trend score collapses, or guidance and news turn negative.
